key_insight: WaspMOT introduces a new long-term multi-object tracking benchmark for ecological footage, targeting identity preservation over minutes-long sequences instead of short clips. It helps reveal whether MOT systems can remain consistent when tracking the same tiny animals for extended periods.
problem_solved: Most MOT benchmarks focus on short videos, which do not properly test long-term tracking and identity maintenance. This paper addresses the need for a dataset that evaluates sustained tracking in realistic, controlled biological experiments.
method: Collected WaspMOT: 10 long video sequences of Trichogramma wasps, each around 12,000 frames long (8+ minutes).
Designed the benchmark specifically for long-term multi-object tracking and identity preservation under controlled ecological conditions.
Provides a harder evaluation setting than standard short-sequence datasets, exposing failure cases such as drift, occlusion recovery, and ID switches over time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, WaspMOT offers a more realistic stress test for tracking models that need to operate reliably over long durations. It can drive the development and evaluation of tracking methods that are better suited for robotics, ecology, surveillance, and any application where identity consistency matters.

paper_title: WaspMOT: A Benchmark for Long-Term Multi-Object Tracking of Trichogramma Wasps
paper_authors: Tomasz Stanczyk, Yuan Gao, Hardik Agarwal, Seongroo Yoon, Tiantao Zhang
